scope: Founding Mode B baselines for the thirteen wave-E2/E3/E4/E5 suites: serp-analysis, competitor-analysis, content-gap-analysis, internal-linking-optimizer, technical-seo-checker, content-refresher, domain-authority-auditor, rank-tracker, performance-reporter, alert-manager, backlink-analyzer, entity-optimizer, memory-management. No suite here has any prior baseline — every record below is a founding datum and zero-regression protection for each suite starts from this file. With the four E1 suites (2026-08-09-e1.json) and the three earlier ones (2026-08-08 / -v2 / 2026-08-09 / -v3), all 20 library skills now hold a Mode B record. READ THE method BLOCK BEFORE THE NUMBERS: two different methods produced these thirteen results and their scores are not comparable.

method.headline: THE CENTRAL FINDING OF THIS BASELINE: ten of the thirteen suites were graded by an agent that executed AND graded while already knowing the expectations (informed-executor). Three were run blind — expectations withheld until each deliverable was written and saved (blind-execute). The results split sharply and the split, not the headline rate, is the finding: informed-executor 96-100% across ten suites; blind 86.2% (memory-management), 85.7% (backlink-analyzer), 62.1% (entity-optimizer). The gap is a property of the METHOD, not of the skills.

informed-executor.definition: One agent read the suite's expectations, then executed the five evals, then graded its own saved outputs. Execute-then-grade order was held (deliverables saved before any grading script existed) and every verdict is quote-backed, but the executor knew what it was going to be graded on while it was writing.
informed-executor.what_it_measures: 'What an expectation-informed executor can satisfy.' NOT 'what a cold fresh session holding only SKILL.md and the prompt would produce.'
informed-executor.upper_bound_statement: THE INFORMED-EXECUTOR SCORES ARE AN UPPER BOUND, NOT A FLOOR. They are optimistically biased by construction and must not be read as evidence that these ten skills behave at 96-100% in real use. The durable artefact from those ten runs is the per-expectation quote-backed evidence and the eval_feedback backlog — not the rate. The rank-tracker runner stated the caveat in its own fragment and it is adopted here for all ten: 'it measures expectations satisfiable by an informed executor and NOT what a cold fresh session with this skill would produce ... treat the per-expectation evidence as the durable artefact and the headline rate as an upper bound.'

blind-execute.definition: For each eval in order the agent read ONLY that eval's prompt and files (extracted up front with jq / a prompts-only projection so no sibling field was on screen), wrote the full deliverable, SAVED it, and only then opened that eval's expectations and expected_output for the first time. No later eval's expectations were read early; deliverables were not edited after their expectations were read.
blind-execute.what_it_measures: Closer to 'what the skill actually produces from prompt + SKILL.md', which is why the 19 FAILs it produced are the most valuable content in this file.

A later run of an informed-executor suite under the blind protocol is NOT a regression even if it scores lower — it is a different measurement (see regression_rule).

regression_rule: Regression = an expectation recorded passing here that fails in a later run of the SAME suite at same-or-later skill version under unchanged expectation wording AND under the same method. the_fail.cause: A DROPPED OBLIGATORY «δεν» IN PASTE-READY CUSTOMER COPY, INVERTING A COMMERCIAL PROMISE. Modern Greek is a strict negative-concord language: the n-word «κανέναν» must be licensed by a preverbal «δεν». «δεσμεύει κανέναν» is ungrammatical as written and a Greek reader resolves it either as a typo or as the affirmative 'it commits somebody' — the exact opposite of the reassurance, in the sentence asking the customer to request a quote. The telegraphic nominal parallel the author reached for («Κόστος μηδέν, δέσμευση καμία.») licenses no finite verb; once a finite verb appears, «δεν» is obligatory.
the_fail.second_defect_in_the_same_eight_word_spa: «κοστίζει μηδέν» is itself a 'costs zero' calque; native is «δεν κοστίζει τίποτα» / «είναι δωρεάν». 'So this is not a stray typo — it is a translation-shaped clause that also lost its negator.'
the_fail.editor_replacement: «— η προσφορά είναι δωρεάν και δεν σας δεσμεύει σε τίποτα.» (equally good: «— η εκτίμηση δεν κοστίζει τίποτα και δεν σας δεσμεύει.»)

coverage.caveat: Coverage is not quality. 10 of the 13 records in this file are informed-executor measurements and 2 of those 10 (serp-analysis, content-refresher) grade outputs whose production was not observed. 'All 20 skills have baselines' is true; 'all 20 skills are measured' is not.

lessons.method_is_the_dominant_variable: Across thirteen suites in one night, the single best predictor of a suite's score was not the skill, its version, its wave, or how many Mode A findings it had absorbed — it was WHETHER THE EXECUTOR HAD SEEN THE EXPECTATIONS. Ten informed suites: 0 FAILs in 282 expectations. Three blind suites: 19 FAILs in 86. Any future baseline that does not record its method is not interpretable.
lessons.blind_protocol_finds_what_mode_a_cannot: The blind runs produced the only two mutually-inconsistent-expectation findings of the wave (entity e2.5/e2.6, memory E3.1/E3.3) and the only deliverable that folded under a stated deadline (backlink e5.3). Mode A adversarial review of the same suites, and ten informed Mode B runs, found neither class. Blindness is not just about honest scores — it surfaces a different KIND of defect.
lessons.fabrication_guard_worked_in_its_designed: Four invented or mis-derived numbers were produced by an executing pass in this wave (entity e1.6 '3rd-century-BC', e3.6 '3,000-strong corpus', e4.6 two wrong per-form counts) and EVERY ONE was caught by the no-fabrication expectation written for it. No fabrication reached a repo file. The ledger F3 guard is doing its job; the observation is about model output under blind conditions, not about a repo regression.
lessons.greek_case_folding_is_a_reproducible_che: Six runs' own checkers independently reproduced the same bug in one night: a lowercase-only Greek pattern missing a sentence-initial «Δεν»/«Κανένα», because grep -i does not case-fold Greek. The published §6 family-5 pattern has the same defect plus a missing nominative «κανείς». The standing lesson exists and is written down — and it was re-broken six times anyway. That argues for a shared, tested Greek matcher rather than a lesson line.
lessons.checker_integrity: 44 checker false verdicts were self-caught across the thirteen runs and ZERO escaped into a recorded verdict. Dominant causes, in order: markdown line-wrapping and blockquote markers defeating substring matches (rank-tracker alone: 6 of 9); negation and quotation frames matched as affirmations — repeatedly, the very sentence an expectation WANTS is the one a naive checker flags; Greek case-folding and inflection; and substring traps ('aGAINSt', «ποτέ» inside «αποτέλεσμα», '95' inside '395'). The ledger F7 print-the-evidence position is the load-bearing control and it held 44 times.
lessons.editor_handoff_worked_once_and_costs_not: The one editor FAIL of the wave was FIRST FLAGGED by a Mode B mechanical checker, which routed it to the editor rather than grading it — and the editor confirmed it. That is the designed handoff working end to end. But the same expectation's demarcation meant the FAIL cost content-refresher zero graded points (26/26 graded expectations still stand). Two suites flagged this shape independently as the carrier-less form ledger F13 was written about. A coordinator decision is owed on whether an editor verdict should bind a scored expectation.
lessons.expectation_bundling_is_the_top_suite_de: Most blind FAILs sit under expectations that bundle four to six separately-checkable clauses into ONE binary verdict (entity e1.1/e2.1/e3.1/e3.5/e5.3, memory E2.4/E5.3, backlink e4.3/e2.1). An output that gets the substance right and omits one denominator is unrepresentable as anything but FAIL, and the recorded FAIL carries none of that shape. The single highest-value suite edit available from this wave is splitting bundled expectations — it appears in the eval_feedback backlog of nearly every suite here.
lessons.operational: A parallel agent OVERWROTE the memory run's checker file mid-run (scratchpad filename collision, second instance after the E1 wave's bare grading.json collision). Suite-prefixed filenames are mandatory; heredoc-only checkers are safer still under concurrency.

what_these_baselines_establish: A founding, per-expectation, quote-backed record for thirteen suites at the named skill versions — the first record any of them has ever had.

A zero-regression floor per suite under the regression_rule, method-scoped: the 19 blind FAILs are the floor for backlink-analyzer, entity-optimizer and memory-management, and a later blind run that fails an expectation passing here IS a regression.
Nineteen concrete, reproducible behavioural gaps with named causes — the most durable content in the file.
Three suite defects (two mutually-inconsistent expectation pairs, one §6 pattern coverage gap) and a 68-item eval_feedback backlog carried verbatim for the suite-repair queue.
Seven binding Greek editor verdicts, one FAIL with its cause, and the §6 carrier work those rulings produced.
what_these_baselines_do_not_establish: THEY DO NOT ESTABLISH THAT TEN SKILLS PERFORM AT 96-100%. Those ten numbers are an upper bound produced by an executor who knew the expectations. The three blind numbers (62.1-86.2%) are the closest thing here to a real-behaviour estimate, and even they carry the coordinator-briefing discount.
They do not license any cross-method comparison, ranking of skills against each other, or a single aggregate pass rate for the wave.

They do not establish cold-session behaviour for ANY skill: the blind runs were blind to expectation wording, not to the launching prompt, which pre-named several traps. A truly cold baseline has not been taken for any skill in this library.
They do not attest that serp-analysis's and content-refresher's deliverables were produced under fresh-session conditions faithful to SKILL.md — those two graders did not observe the execution.
They do not establish Greek quality for six of the thirteen suites: those artefacts are recorded on their mechanical layer only and have not been seen by the binding editor.
They carry no variance estimate: every eval ran exactly once, so a single re-run could move any of these rates and nothing here says by how much.

They do not measure the skills against each other's difficulty: entity-optimizer's 62.1% is not evidence that entity-optimizer is the worst skill in the library — it is the hardest-graded suite run under the strictest method, and its expectations bundle more clauses per verdict than most.
They do not close the informed/blind question: re-running the ten informed suites blind is the only way to learn what those skills actually do, and that work is not done.
